PRODUCT OVERVIEW

Confirm the container before choosing the chassis.

For port, depot and logistics-hub container movements, start with the container dimensions, loaded weight and loading conditions. A 20-foot or 40-foot designation is only a starting point; confirm locking positions, vehicle dimensions and the tractor before deciding compatibility.

The six listed container semi-trailers include two- and three-axle Chuyuan and Xiangqi models. For example, EHJ9350TJZE has two axles and a gross mass of 35000 kg, while EHJ9400TJZE has three axles and a gross mass of 40000 kg. Similar appearance does not mean identical specifications.

APPLICATION & SELECTION

Turn your application into selection criteria

Discuss the actual transport task first, then check the corresponding model and equipment.

01

Container and locking positions

Provide the container type, dimensions, corner-fitting or locking-position drawing, and whether the task involves single or twin containers. Vehicle length alone does not establish compatibility.

02

Compare two and three axles

Compare gross mass, rated payload and curb mass alongside axle count. JDV9350TJZE is a two-axle model; JDV9390TJZE has three axles. Use the complete model code when discussing a configuration.

03

Tractor and operating environment

Provide tractor coupling information, loading equipment, route and operating region. State any stake, curtain-side or box-body requirement separately; a bare chassis specification should not be reused for a different body.

Need an open deck or sideboards? Compare flatbed and drop-side models.

PREPARE YOUR ENQUIRY

Prepare these four details for your enquiry

Specific information helps us compare models and configurations. Price, availability and the final proposal are confirmed through the enquiry.

Container information

Container type, exterior dimensions, loaded container weight, and corner-fitting or locking-position details.

Loading and combinations

Single- or twin-container requirements, handling equipment, operating sites and route.

Tractor compatibility

Tractor model, fifth-wheel and coupling information, and operating region.

Model and options

Preferred approval model, axle count, tire and suspension requirements, quantity and intended in-service date.

You can start with the cargo and operating task; sales will help identify a model and configuration. If a model is already chosen, provide its complete code rather than only the category.
